Hello. And thank you for letting me the opportunity to speak to you today. My name is Ashley Carter and my role at Serita's Manager or Business Development.
I work with our local companies to provide the programs and services that they need to grow.
As you know, the Business Development incentive is an important part of the value proposition for doing business in Saskatoon.
There are many companies that have successfully received the incentive and continue to choose our city to grow and expand their business.
I'm confident that you'll see even more quality applications and dedicated businesses benefiting from this program in the years to come.
This afternoon I'm excited to speak to you on an application for the Business Development incentive submitted by hinge designs, a local manufacturing company who is poised for growth.

Specializing in custom cabinetry for residential development, hinge designs has grown from a small operation into a thriving business that employs 25 people and serves diverse clients from homeowners to home builders and large scale multifamily developments.
The owner of hinge designs is an experienced entrepreneur who sees a bright future for the residential cabinet industry and has a long term vision for growth and expansion.
With the demand for residential cabinetry increasing due to continued population growth and new housing starts, a healthy pipeline of projects is in front of hinge designs.
Consumer preference for locally sourced high quality cabinetry have made room for manufacturers like this to grow their operations in our city.

Starting with a 22,000 square foot facility in Saskatoon's north end, hinge designs will increase their production capacity through this expansion, more than 100% and grow their full-time employee base by over 30%.
These changes will allow for new efficiencies and the capacity to implement advanced technologies to further increase productivity.
Sereda is confident that hinge designs 5.5 million dollar investment in the creation of eight new full-time equivalent roles will be an impactful contribution to Saskatoon's development.
Their application meets all listed eligibility criteria within the Business Development incentive policy and has been thoroughly vetted by Sereda's incentive review advisory committee.
Construction for the facilities set to begin in Q2 of this year and the applicant expects to be fully operational in this new space by the end of Q1 in 2026.
This project is well aligned with Saskatoon's economic priorities from creating new jobs to supporting the growing housing sector.
The application reflects the kind of sustainable, locally driven growth that the Business Development incentive is designed to support.
In closing, hinge designs is a company rooted in Saskatoon's economy with a strong future ahead.
With this information, Sereda is recommending approval of hinge designs business development incentive application.

Thank you, Mr. Chair, and this one's a little bit longer of an introduction as it does have some history.
This report is in response to an outstanding resolution regarding the city's possibility of a recovery or clawback clause as a related to the Maven water and environment incentive agreement.
The incentive agreement for Maven was approved on May 11, 2020, with 2022 being the first year that the agreement was provided.
Serita completed their annual audit in 2023 and 2024.
Both years indicating that Maven had not met their FTE goals as required in the incentive agreement.
But recommended continuation of the abatement on the basis that Maven was actively recruiting positions, including utilization of a recruitment agency.
And the shortfall was more related to a difficulty in finding the required skill set.
In each year, the abatement was approved to continue with the caveat that the FTE shortfall be remedied within nine months as allowed for in the policy, however it was never met.
In January of 2025, administration was informed that Maven had been acquired by an Alberta-based company named Integrated Sustainability.
Further administration received a letter from Integrated Sustainability on March 17, 2025, seeking a further exception to the FTE criteria indicating a plan to fulfill the required complement.
On April 29, 2025, we received further correspondence from Integrated Sustainability indicating that they were withdrawing their request as they would not be able to meet the FTE requirements.
The report in front of committee today was written on that most written on the basis of that most recent correspondence that Integrated Sustainability was withdrawing from the program.
As such, the report outlines that administration's intent was to pursue the recovery of approximately $54,000 in previously provided abatements.

Since writing this report and complicating matters is a letter received by Integrated Sustainability just yesterday and attached in the agenda which highlights another change in their request to be reconsidered in the program again moving forward.
With this new correspondence, the administration's perspective is the committee would essentially have three options today.

Option one would be of committee feels like there is not enough information today you could request a report back that would be brought forward to August outlining the various options based on this new request from Integrated Sustainability.
Or two of committee feels like there is enough information today to make a decision.
There are several sub-options that could be made including denying the request and directing administration to proceed with recovery efforts,
or approving Integrated Sustainabilities request to continue with Mayvans previously approved incentive.
With that, the report was originally written as information, but due to the new information that administration would be seeking some direction from committee on how they would like to proceed.

As outlined in the report, the business improvement districts are currently required to get an annual external audit done of their financial statements unless their revenues are less than $250,000 in which they are allowed to complete an annual review engagement.
Consisting with the Non-profit Corporations Act of 1995.
This currently allows for the 33rd Street and Southern Business Improvement District to offer a review engagement as opposed to a full audit.
The Non-profit Corporations Act was updated in 2022 and as part of this update, the threshold requirement for audits was also adjusted.
Specifically, organizations with annual revenue up to 500,000 could now opt for review engagement as opposed to an audit and organizations with under 100,000.
And revenue no longer required an audit or a review engagement at all.

While the business improvement districts are not technically a not for profit, this legislation provided valuable reference in establishing the city's original audit requirements and balancing the cost of an audit engagement versus the assurance level required by the city.
The report includes several options for committee to consider.
The administration is recommending to increase the option to elect for a review engagement from the current $250,000 threshold.
$2,500,000 to align with the Not for Profit Corporations Act.
This would allow for the Riversdale and Broadway Business Improvement District to opt for a review engagement in addition to the 33rd Street and Southern Business Improvement District.
The Downtown Business Improvement District with annual revenues over 1 million would still be required to conduct an annual audit engagement.

The administration field that proposed revision to the business improvement bylaw would provide the city with a reasonable level of assurance over the business improvement districts financial statements,
provide and provide potential for cost savings for the bids and align with the original decision to establish the $250,000 threshold based on the Not for Profit Corporations Act.
